author: Orienta
name: Large features only (heavy smoothing)
notes:
Heavy smoothing: groups the map into a few large, chemically distinct areas.

GOOD FOR: coarse second-phase fields, segregation bands, eutectic regions - anything several micrometres across that you want as one clean area rather than as speckle.
NOT FOR: fine precipitates. Anything thinner than about 5 um is averaged into its surroundings and will not appear at all. If you cannot find a particle you know is there, this preset is the reason - use one of the 2.5 um starters instead.

This is a sensible starting point you can then correct. It is not the correct answer.

SMOOTHING is 5 um, a physical width, so it means the same analysis at any step size. Measured on the SampleB test scan (0.5 um step) that is a 10 px box: 50 connected pieces with a median size of 28 px, against 74 pieces with a median of 3 px at 2.5 um. Coherence 0.908.

CANDIDATE PHASES are whatever your CIF library holds; this preset pins no list, so it is convenient and not reproducible. Pin the list in your own copy.
